messages:
mari: Heads-up — NA-east prefetched pool 'na-east-prefetch' showing a sustained tail p95 spike for short chat gen since ~09:12 UTC. Services routing there see ~3x latency.

oncall-bot: ALERT: egress_interface_errors on na-east-prefetch (09:14 UTC) — 73% packet drops on nic-eth2 across 6 nodes.

raj: Seeing a lot of `device grpc stall` in the runtime logs for those nodes. Might be backpressure from egress queue filling up due to prefetch traffic.

lina: Is this the continuous-prefetch feature we rolled last week? Could be generating lots of small outbound fetches and saturating the NIC egress queue.

mari: Yes — `continuous-prefetch=on` on that pool. I can flip it off on the pool config, but need someone to approve a traffic shift while we do mitigation.

vishal: Approve. Prioritize latency. Do we have spare capacity in NA-east spare pool or should we route to NA-west?

raj: NA-east-spare has 8 reserved GPUs idle. I'd prefer to move traffic there to avoid cross-region egress. Quick plan: (1) disable prefetch on na-east-prefetch nodes, (2) shift 70% traffic to na-east-spare with a gradual 30s ramp, (3) scale na-east-spare to full if we see load.

mari: On it. Command I'll run:```sh
# disable pool prefetch flag
rdctl pool update na-east-prefetch --set continuous_prefetch=false
# adjust routing policy
rdctl route set traffic --from na-east-prefetch --to na-east-spare --percent 70 --step 30s
```

deploy-bot: deploy job started by mari at 09:18:11 UTC — change: pool config update -> continuous_prefetch=false

mari: Disabled prefetch on 6 nodes. Kicking traffic shift now.

deploy-bot: route update in progress -> 70% to na-east-spare (30s steps).

lina: Adding network-level mitigation: lowering egress queue depth on the offending nodes and enabling BPF backpressure drop to favor control traffic. Doing that now (2 nodes per batch).

raj: After first step we see p95 drop from 620ms -> 310ms on affected services. Packet drops falling to ~12%. Good sign.

vishal: Nice. Keep the shift until we confirm stable for 10m, then we can bring 30% back if the NICs behave. Also let's keep histograms for model batch size — prefetch was creating many tiny batches.

mari: Captured a short log snippet before/after:```
[09:16:02] runtime: batcher: emitted 82 tiny batches in 60s (avg seq_len 16)
[09:20:30] runtime: batcher: emitted 18 batches in 60s (avg seq_len 64)
```

lina: Those tiny batches explain CPU/io overhead + more egress calls. Prefetch off reduces small-batch churn.

raj: Cost note: moving 70% to na-east-spare and scaling may add ~0.35 commit-hours per minute; estimate ~$110 extra for the hour. Flagging for finance.

vishal: Accepted — prefer short cost vs degradation. Please capture the exact minutes for billing reconciliation.

mari: Monitoring dashboards — p95 is now ~290-330ms, error rate stable. Will keep 70% shift for 15m, then evaluate.

lina: Plan for next steps: (A) investigate prefetch hot-path concurrency limits and rate-limiter, (B) add guardrail to avoid cross-NIC egress saturation (egress qdisc + token-bucket), (C) add e2e test simulating prefetch at scale.

raj: I'll open a follow-up ticket for autoscaler tuning — current autoscaler reacts to queue length too slowly for this pattern. Might need a short-term reactive policy for NIC errors.

mari: FYI I pulled a snapshot of node NIC stats and pushed to the incident ticket: https://redwood.test/incident/INC-2187 (contains `tcp_drop` + `tx_queue_len`).

deploy-bot: route update complete at 09:22:39 UTC.

mari: Observability: setting a paged alert if p95 > 500ms for more than 2m.

vishal: Thanks everyone. We'll keep this thread for postmortem notes. Re-enable prefetch only after we have rate-limits + token-bucket on the prefetcher.

lina: Noted — recording RCA action items now.

mari: Closing immediate mitigation. Will update in 30m with final numbers. :rocket:
